name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +25 Democratic partisan lean after redistricting
Haynes' large fundraising edge ($420K vs $17K) plus $200K outside support
model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals give Democrats a roughly 25-point structural edge, and Haynes has vastly out-raised Jackson with outside backing, while markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold. Nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Jackson within single digits, or major outside spending against Haynes, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open Dallas-area seat that redistricting made solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 25 points toward Democrats. Frederick Haynes III enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $420,000 and holding nearly $120,000 on hand, supplemented by about $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with about $1,200 remaining, leaving little capacity to compete.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong structural lean and the lopsided resource gap, both pointing to a comfortable Democratic victory.
